paragraphs: In A Blink sells a wireless data link for transit vehicles, described as a drop-in replacement for Wi-Fi that is up to 200 times faster. The point of it is that an operator can offload all the data from a bus or a railcar in minutes instead of hours.

Instead of radio, the patent pending approach uses what the company calls Quantum Communication technology to make Virtual Fibre Optics possible. The optical link works on invisible light. An on-board router adds 4G, LTE and 5G cellular with dual-SIM support for real-time transmissions. The result the company describes is that data is stored at the command center instead of on the vehicles.

The data in question is what transit vehicles collect as they operate, covering telemetry, fare collection, health monitoring, and security. Among the benefits the company claims is quicker resolution of crimes and claims through reliable access to data. It also says the system uses existing infrastructure and operational rules to fit into an agency's IT architecture.
